correctness.rationale: Exact input supports (2,2,6,4,4,6,4,4,4,2,2) imply the eleven necessary output quotas. The hand proof forces two prescribed top-two prefixes, then the third elements and the remaining ranking, and contradicts the required comparison 1 before 5. Three explicit witnesses directly meet each two-axiom conjunction. Repeating all six input rankings preserves normalized quotas; adding universally bottom-ranked candidates preserves pairwise witnesses and yields restriction to the five-candidate contradiction. The complete standard-library checker validates all 295240 three-order multisets (5,44,6 pairwise, 0 triple) and independently tests all three pair witnesses using threshold quantifiers. No finite experiment is presented as proof for the unbounded family.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Theorem 3 of the motivating work supplies profiles lacking any pairwise proportional output, which cannot imply a pairwise-feasible three-way separation for the same profile. Theorem 4 establishes joint existence under single-peakedness, while this witness is unrestricted. Earlier rank aggregation studies one output, and committee PSC selects candidates rather than complete rankings.

originality.rationale: The 2026 motivating paper has individual existence, a much larger intrinsic pairwise-impossibility witness, and simultaneous existence on single-peaked profiles, but no claim that all three fairness axioms can fail jointly even when every two are jointly achievable. The new profile satisfies pairwise proportionality and both its two-axiom combinations, so intrinsic nonexistence of pairwise output does not entail it. Its replicated/padded family is also not implied. Other rank-aggregation and committee PSC frameworks have different objects/guarantees. Targeted published-results and primary-literature searches found no dominating theorem; residual priority risk is acknowledged.

value.rationale: The motivating framework proves distinct independent guarantees and structured-domain joint guarantees, leaving a natural question whether the three independently meaningful proportionality criteria can be combined. An explicit pairwise-compatible but triple-incompatible instance distinguishes genuine three-way obstruction from failure of a single axiom. The construction extends to every replicated six-voter multiple and any candidate count at least five, giving a structural failure mechanism rather than an unmotivated one-off numerical anomaly. Exact pairwise feasibility counts further document the tension.
